notes.title: Happy New Year
notes.notes:
Hello Dear Community,

As   the   year   is   coming   to   the   end,   we’d   like   to   make   some   updates   on
Fishkeeper’s development. Notwithstanding all the rumors, the project is not
dead and we haven’t abandoned it. We are just still in need of funding, seeking
opportunities to make a fully playable game. It’s much harder as we are an
independent team, working on our own projects in our free time only. Stay tuned
for the next year – we promise that as soon as we get a chance to develop the
game to the fullest extent, we’ll let you know.


And we wish you a happy New Year too. Take care

notes.title: [DEV DIARY: KICKSTARTER]
notes.notes:
[b][url=https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/psos/fishkeeper]Fishkeeper on Kickstarter[/url]
[/b]
[b]Watch the new Fishkeeper Kickstarter trailer:
[/b]
[previewyoutube=em23OB0Wn_Q;full][/previewyoutube]

Hello guys,

there’s a day when we’re setting off to reach an extremely important milestone on the way to the full game version.

As you know, Fishkeeper is a big project that involves such things like advanced AI, web mechanisms, good quality graphics and animations, and much more similar stuff.

As you may’ve heard, the costs of all that works are truly expensive and often counted in hundreds of thousand $. That’s the moment when our team’s own funds are out. We don’t want to seek protection from big publishers and stock investors as they would gain direct control on Fishkeeper and strictly limit our vision and ability to create the project together with you guys, basing on the community’s ideas. If we sell Fishkeeper, we would stop being truly ‘indie’, and the game wouldn’t be that good as we want.

Today we’re launching Fishkeeper’s fundraising on Kickstarter. To be honest, that’s our last chance to get the money needed to complete the game. People say it’s very hard to collect the sum on time, but I think valuable projects just worth it, so I hope so much that my indie game dev mission is not yet wasted.

I also kindly ask you and other players for whom the idea of high-realistic aquarium simulation is close to their heart to support the production of Fishkeeper with some funds. We’re highly grateful for every single cent paid in. Of course, we prepared different digital rewards for your gratification. It’s a very significant move for us as it’s about Fishkeeper’s fate. If we manage to collect at least part of the game budget, it will become possible to continue the development and finally finish it.

You can support us also in another way, like sharing the link to the fundraising campaign with your friends on Facebook or Twitter. We highly appreciate any effort to help Fishkeeper come into being.

Many thanks in advance,

Yours
Devs

notes.title: Fishkeeper aims to become The Sims for aquarium hobbyists
notes.notes:
When Blinkclick Games, a small indie studio based in Krakow, first sat down together to work out what the plan for its first game would be, the developers agreed: they wanted to make something that was innovative, with "completely new mechanics". It would involve a complex economics simulation and highly realistic AI, but instead of making a flashy FPS or a new RTS game, the studio turned to something its members knew from first-hand experience. They decided to make a game about fish.

Fishkeeper is, put as simply as possible, an aquarium simulator. And while it's not the first or only aquarium game, Blinkclick CEO and creative director Piotr Soska tells us it's different in that it's built on as much real-world information about fish, their habitats, and aquariums as the studio has been able to lay hands on since it began creating the game.

"Our producer Jarek says he used to be seriously involved in the aquarium hobby in his teenage [years], but one day moving to another place forced him to throw away his tank and give his fish to friends," Soska says. "For a long time after he couldn't even sleep without the noise of the filter and aerator in his bedroom."

notes.title: First gameplay video on IGN!
notes.notes:
A month has passed after Fishkeeper was announced in the media and the first very early gameplay film was published on the IGN YouTube channel. The gameplay shows the basic building process of a fish tank and early purchase and deleting mechanics. Keep in mind that it is a very early phase of the game development - it’s about a month from the time we started creating the proper game. Treat it rather as proof we don’t get too comfortable and move forward!

Tell us what you think about it - we appreciate your feedback.

As the game will have some progress later, we will be publishing new materials presenting new game features and add them here to the community as a dev diary, so stay launched.

notes.title: Fishkeeper, the most cyberpunk way to keep fish, is coming in 2021
notes.notes:
The year is 2020 and you have one mission: making some cool-looking fish as happy as possible. That's the basic idea behind Fishkeeper, the most cyberpunk way to keep fish. It's on the way to Steam and set to launch at the end of 2021.

For now though, you can have a look at a preliminary gameplay video of Fishkeeper. It's a life simulation game with some tycoon elements: you'll set up an aquarium, deck it out with sand, equipment, and scenery, and then populate it with your favourite kinds of fish. In the video below, you'll see that you can choose from freshwater or saltwater species, and there's a wide selection of accessories, plants, and toys to use to make your fish tank an interesting place to live.

Fishkeeper even goes beyond the normal aquarist experience by giving you a way to actually hang out with your fishy friends - plop in a submersible drone called a 'bathyscale' and you can putter around among the colourful fish you've added to your tank.
